answer-er27-25-miso.point: MISO says LARS responds to the show cause order and should not wait for the large load cost reforms due November 16.
answer-er27-25-miso.quote: such a delay would frustrate the goals of the Show Cause Order and needlessly sacrifice the benefits of critical reforms for ratepayers and stakeholders without corresponding benefit.

answer-er27-25-miso.point: MISO says the Local Resource Zone fits its system and the order invited tailoring the proximity definition.
answer-er27-25-miso.quote: MISO is expanding upon the Commission's definition to fit its needs and resource adequacy construct.

answer-er27-25-miso.point: MISO describes its zone test as electrically proximate plus because it rewards close siting and also serves pairs farther apart.
answer-er27-25-miso.quote: MISO's LRZ approach thus can be considered an "electrically proximate plus" construct

answer-er27-25-miso.point: MISO says LARS creates no new cost shift, and the Transmission Customer stays liable for assigned projects even if the load never starts service.
answer-er27-25-miso.quote: LARS does not create any new cost shift opportunities, but LARS does mitigate risks that already exist.

answer-er27-25-miso.point: MISO and the Transmission Owners will file pro forma cost recovery agreements by November 16, 2026, and MISO would accept a compliance directive to fold them into LARS.
answer-er27-25-miso.quote: MISO is willing to accept a compliance directive requiring such a filing should the Commission deem this necessary.

answer-er27-25-miso.point: MISO says LARS will not take headroom from DPP queue projects because LARS models are built on the existing MTEP model.
answer-er27-25-miso.quote: each LARS study cycle model will be built based on the existing MTEP model, which would not remove any available headroom from active DPP queue projects

answer-er27-25-miso.point: MISO rejects the gatekeeper charge: only Transmission Customers have been able to submit EPR requests, and an unpaired generator would make LARS speculative.
answer-er27-25-miso.quote: LARS is a load-driven process, and an Interconnection Customer cannot require a Transmission Customer to scope their Transmission Service request around a generator they have not chosen to pair with.

answer-er27-25-miso.point: MISO opposes a sunset date but commits to post pair data each cycle and to review usage regularly.
answer-er27-25-miso.quote: MISO commits to publicly post, at the beginning of each LARS cycle, information on each LARS generation/load pair's POI and POW

answer-er27-25-miso.point: MISO defends the 200 MW floor and the 15-year pairing as ways to keep LARS for the largest, committed pairs.
answer-er27-25-miso.quote: The 15-year minimum pairing of the generation and load pairs in LARS is a necessary aspect of ensuring certainty for MISO

protest-er27-25-acp-srea.point: The trades say LARS goes further than ERAS: permanent, uncapped, untethered to a resource adequacy need, and run through the load-serving entity.
protest-er27-25-acp-srea.quote: It is permanent and uncapped. It is untethered to any identified resource adequacy need.

protest-er27-25-acp-srea.point: They say making the LSE the applicant gives LSEs gatekeeper control over a jurisdictional interconnection process.
protest-er27-25-acp-srea.quote: LARS is unduly discriminatory because it makes the LSE the gatekeeper of a Commission-jurisdictional generator interconnection process

protest-er27-25-acp-srea.point: They contend the show cause order did not call for a permanent expedited queue and described interim service until ERIS or NRIS.
protest-er27-25-acp-srea.quote: The Show Cause Order did not direct MISO to create a separate, permanent, expedited generator interconnection queue.

protest-er27-25-acp-srea.point: They cite bounded precedents: PJM RRI at 50 projects and MISO ERAS at 68 requests ending by August 31, 2027.
protest-er27-25-acp-srea.quote: The revised MISO ERAS process is capped at 68 requests and sunsets no later than August 31, 2027

protest-er27-25-acp-srea.point: They argue same-LRZ pairing grants broad injection rights to generators that need not be operationally tied to the load.
protest-er27-25-acp-srea.quote: its same-LRZ pairing grants broad priority injection rights to generators that need not be operationally tied to the load.

protest-er27-25-acp-srea.point: They note LARS studies exclude DPP requests lacking executed GIAs, which they say shifts capacity and costs away from DPP customers.
protest-er27-25-acp-srea.quote: exclude DPP Interconnection Requests that lack an executed Generator Interconnection

protest-er27-25-acp-srea.point: They say MISO has not shown LARS meets the independent entity variation standard.
protest-er27-25-acp-srea.quote: MISO has not shown that LARS satisfies the independent entity variation standard.

protest-er27-25-acp-srea.point: As a fallback, they request clarification that the same-LRZ test uses the point of interconnection.
protest-er27-25-acp-srea.quote: the relevant location is the applicable POI to the MISO Transmission System rather than the physical location of the Generating Facility

comments-er27-25-alliant-consumers.point: The utilities support a study process that handles generation paired with large load together.
comments-er27-25-alliant-consumers.quote: support the need for an interconnection process that facilitates the timely study of generation paired with an associated large load(s) to arrive at optimized transmission solutions.

comments-er27-25-alliant-consumers.point: Joint planning can avoid duplicate or costly upgrades and lower customer costs.
comments-er27-25-alliant-consumers.quote: eliminate duplicative or unnecessarily expensive upgrades, and help deliver lower-cost outcomes for customers.

comments-er27-25-alliant-consumers.point: They cite MISO's goal of finishing the parallel study in about 120 days.
comments-er27-25-alliant-consumers.quote: with the objective of completing the process within approximately 120 days.

comments-er27-25-alliant-consumers.point: They back strong readiness requirements to keep speculative projects out.
comments-er27-25-alliant-consumers.quote: Strong readiness requirements are therefore an appropriate safeguard against speculative projects consuming scarce study resources

comments-er27-25-alliant-consumers.point: They expect MISO to keep working with stakeholders on how projects retain interconnection rights over time.
comments-er27-25-alliant-consumers.quote: providing greater certainty regarding the conditions under which projects may retain interconnection rights over time.

comments-er27-25-arkansas-psc.point: The Arkansas PSC supports LARS and joins the Mississippi and Louisiana commissions' comments.
comments-er27-25-arkansas-psc.quote: The APSC supports MISO's filing to establish the LARS process, and agrees with the comments made by the Mississippi Public Service Commission and the Louisiana Public Service Commission.

comments-er27-25-arkansas-psc.point: It says LARS aligns with the show cause order's requirements.
comments-er27-25-arkansas-psc.quote: AR agrees that LARS is a reasonable response to and aligns with the requirements of the Commission's Show Cause Order.

protest-er27-25-bloom.point: Bloom supports LARS and its December 2 effective date, and protests only the 200 MW minimum.
protest-er27-25-bloom.quote: Bloom protests one element only: the 200 MW minimum load size.

protest-er27-25-bloom.point: Bloom says MISO lowered the threshold from 250 MW to 200 MW without new analysis.
protest-er27-25-bloom.quote: MISO presents no EPR results or other grid impact study for 200 MW, and none for loads below it.

protest-er27-25-bloom.point: The 200 MW floor departs from the 50 MW definition in the show cause order and in MISO's pending IRR filing.
protest-er27-25-bloom.quote: The Show Cause Order identified a reasonable large load definition as a single-site commercial or industrial customer with peak load of 50 MW or greater.

protest-er27-25-bloom.point: Bloom argues paired loads below 200 MW are similarly situated and that the ten-pair cap already focuses each study cycle.
protest-er27-25-bloom.quote: And the ten-pair cap, not a size threshold, already preserves the focus of each study cycle.

protest-er27-25-bloom.point: Bloom says the right screen is connection to the Transmission System, so LARS should cover loads of 50 MW or more.
protest-er27-25-bloom.quote: LARS should therefore apply to loads of 50 MW or more that connect to the Transmission System.

protest-er27-25-bloom.point: If the minimum falls, Bloom asks FERC to conform the 200 MW generation-side minimum in Section 3.12.2.
protest-er27-25-bloom.quote: it should direct a conforming change to Section 3.12.2, which separately requires at least 200 MW of Network Resource Interconnection Service at each Point of Interconnection.

comments-er27-25-dte.point: DTE Electric supports LARS as a reasonable way to evaluate load additions and paired generation.
comments-er27-25-dte.quote: DTE Electric supports MISO's proposal and believes the LARS framework represents a reasonable approach to evaluating the transmission, operational, and resource adequacy impacts

comments-er27-25-dte.point: Studying load and generation together can show different impacts than stand-alone studies.
comments-er27-25-dte.quote: jointly planned and electrically proximate resources may produce materially different system impacts than traditional stand-alone studies.

comments-er27-25-dte.point: DTE points to deposit, size, site control and pairing requirements as safeguards against speculative requests.
comments-er27-25-dte.quote: Participating projects must satisfy applicable deposit, minimum size, site control, and commercial operation requirements.

comments-er27-25-dte.point: DTE notes any eligible entity may be the interconnection customer for the generation.
comments-er27-25-dte.quote: permitting the interconnection customer responsible for the generation component to be any eligible entity

comments-er27-25-entergy-cleco.point: Entergy and Cleco support LARS for loads over 200 MW that have identified new generation.
comments-er27-25-entergy-cleco.quote: enable MISO to expeditiously review the interconnection needs of large loads over 200 MW that have identified new generation resources to support their needs.

comments-er27-25-entergy-cleco.point: They say MISO DPP cycles of four years or longer leave utilities without a timely path to interconnect generation built for new load.
comments-er27-25-entergy-cleco.quote: MISO's DPP cycles have taken four years or longer to reach completion

comments-er27-25-entergy-cleco.point: They say LARS can reach a reliable outcome in about 120 days, which separate processes cannot.
comments-er27-25-entergy-cleco.quote: produce a reliable outcome in approximately 120 days.

comments-er27-25-entergy-cleco.point: They argue a permanent LARS gives the certainty needed to site and finance load and generation pairings.
comments-er27-25-entergy-cleco.quote: Making LARS a permanent process is appropriate because it provides needed, long-term regulatory and financial certainty

comments-er27-25-entergy-cleco.point: They ask FERC to judge LARS under the independent entity variation standard.
comments-er27-25-entergy-cleco.quote: The Commission should evaluate LARS under the

comments-er27-25-entergy-cleco.point: They list the limits: ten pairs per period, three periods a year, 150 percent ceiling, $250,000 deposit, three-year commercial operation date and same Local Resource Zone.
comments-er27-25-entergy-cleco.quote: only ten generation/load pairs per study period will be evaluated, with three periods per year.

protest-er27-25-google.point: Google supports the LARS concept but protests that MISO filed it without protections against cost shifting.
protest-er27-25-google.quote: MISO has filed LARS without accompanying and necessary protections against cost shifting, which prevents the Commission from finding that LARS is just and reasonable.

protest-er27-25-google.point: Upgrades for load-caused violations are classed as Baseline Reliability or Other projects, whose costs are recovered from all network customers in the pricing zone.
protest-er27-25-google.quote: the costs of those project types are recovered from all network customers in a Transmission Pricing Zone.

protest-er27-25-google.point: Overallocated headroom would be fixed through a future MTEP project, and residential customers could bear that cost.
protest-er27-25-google.quote: residential and other commercial customers could be left holding the bag for transmission projects needed to interconnect LARS generators

protest-er27-25-google.point: Google suggests more conservative study assumptions, such as counting DPP requests at Decision Point II, to avoid overallocation.
protest-er27-25-google.quote: LARS could be modified to use more conservative assumptions

protest-er27-25-google.point: MISO plans to file the pro forma cost shifting agreement by November 16, 2026, so the record lacks it today.
protest-er27-25-google.quote: the cost shifting agreement will be submitted in a separate section 205 filing by November 16, 2026

protest-er27-25-google.point: Google offers two options: reject with direction to refile with protections, or accept, suspend and consolidate with the MISO show cause proceeding.
protest-er27-25-google.quote: the Commission could accept and suspend the proposal and consolidate it with the MISO Large Load Show Cause proceeding

protest-er27-25-google.point: Google says routing applications through load-serving entities risks undue discrimination against independent generators.
protest-er27-25-google.quote: LARS opens the door to undue discrimination and could undermine core open access principles by making load-serving entities ("LSEs") the gatekeepers of the LARS process.

protest-er27-25-consumer-advocates.point: The protesters oppose exempting or partly exempting about 30 GW of existing load from MISO's large load reliability requirements.
protest-er27-25-consumer-advocates.quote: MISO is proposing to fully or partially exempt approximately 30 gigawatts of existing load from the Large Load Interconnection Reliability Requirements.

protest-er27-25-consumer-advocates.point: They say LARS does not address the show cause order's cost-shifting concerns, which MISO defers to filings due by November 16.
protest-er27-25-consumer-advocates.quote: MISO's LARS Process does not address the Commission's concerns regarding cost-shifting expressed in the Show Cause Order.

protest-er27-25-consumer-advocates.point: Violations seen in the load study or in both studies go to Baseline Reliability or Other projects, which are allocated zonally.
protest-er27-25-consumer-advocates.quote: The LARS Process does not assign the cost of all network upgrades to the cost-causer.

protest-er27-25-consumer-advocates.point: They say a same-Local-Resource-Zone test departs from the order's two-substation example of electrically proximate.
protest-er27-25-consumer-advocates.quote: MISO's LRZ proposal does not meaningfully engage with the Show Cause Order.

protest-er27-25-consumer-advocates.point: They argue LARS studies generators before DPP projects that have waited through multiple phases.
protest-er27-25-consumer-advocates.quote: In effect, any LARS project will be studied before the DPP projects that have waited through multiple phases of study.

protest-er27-25-consumer-advocates.point: They ask FERC to let them address cost impacts across all MISO section 205 filings in the section 206 show cause docket.
protest-er27-25-consumer-advocates.quote: The Joint Protestors should be permitted to address the cost-shifting impacts, transparency issues, and other consumer protection issues raised in MISO's Section 205 filings as a whole

comments-er27-25-southern-regulators.point: The regulators describe LARS as meant to address the show cause order finding on electrically proximate large loads.
comments-er27-25-southern-regulators.quote: The LARS proposal also is intended to address the Commission's June 18, 2026 Show Cause Order finding that MISO's Tariff may be unjust and unreasonable

comments-er27-25-southern-regulators.point: LARS coordinates and speeds study of loads above 200 MW and the generation identified for them.
comments-er27-25-southern-regulators.quote: coordinate and expedite the analyses needed to interconnect large loads above 200 MW and the new generation resources identified to support that new load.

comments-er27-25-southern-regulators.point: Joint study can cut upgrade needs and costs, and LARS studies pairs in 120 days.
comments-er27-25-southern-regulators.quote: LARS provides for a 120-day parallel study of eligible large loads and their paired generation resources.

comments-er27-25-southern-regulators.point: They say permanence supplies the certainty needed to site and finance pairings.
comments-er27-25-southern-regulators.quote: Making LARS a permanent process is reasonable because it provides certainty needed to site and finance large load-and-generation pairings.

comments-er27-25-southern-regulators.point: They list the caps and eligibility rules that deter speculative requests.
comments-er27-25-southern-regulators.quote: including a 150% generation to load ceiling, a $250,000 deposit, a three-year commercial operation date, and a same-Local-Resource-Zone requirement.

protest-er27-25-seia-united.point: Only the LARS Associated Transmission Customer, often a load-serving entity, can start an application.
protest-er27-25-seia-united.quote: The LARS Associated Transmission Customer is the only party that may initiate the LARS Application.

protest-er27-25-seia-united.point: They say independent producers can join only if the utility competitor lets them, with no duty to submit.
protest-er27-25-seia-united.quote: Yes, independent power producers can participate in the LARS process

protest-er27-25-seia-united.point: They ask FERC to reject LARS and direct a refiling that lets any qualified market participant apply directly to MISO.
protest-er27-25-seia-united.quote: reject the LARS proposal, on the grounds that the proposal is unduly discriminatory

protest-er27-25-seia-united.point: A generator whose paired load leaves in the first fifteen years can lose its LLGIA and must re-enter the DPP.
protest-er27-25-seia-united.quote: the generator's LLGIA ultimately will be terminated and the generator must obtain new Interconnection Service through the Definitive Planning Process (DPP) to continue operating.

protest-er27-25-seia-united.point: MISO offers only a transition period of up to one year, which they contrast with SPP's five-year HILLGA approach.
protest-er27-25-seia-united.quote: MISO proposes only a temporary transition period of up to one year

protest-er27-25-seia-united.point: They say LARS studies leave out queued DPP projects without executed GIAs, so the two processes use different assumptions.
protest-er27-25-seia-united.quote: MISO specifically states that LARS studies will not include interconnection requests currently in the generator interconnection queue that have not executed GIAs.

protest-er27-25-seia-united.point: In the alternative, they ask FERC to clarify that the Associated Transmission Customer must apply the same standards and timelines it uses for its own projects.
protest-er27-25-seia-united.quote: the Commission expects the LARS Associated Transmission Customer to apply the same submission standards and timelines it applies to its own similarly situated projects.

protest-er27-25-clean-energy-advocates.point: The groups say LARS is a new permanent parallel process that shifts costs, creates reliability concerns and allows discrimination.
protest-er27-25-clean-energy-advocates.quote: MISO's LARS proposal is a new, permanent parallel interconnection study process that will shift costs from large loads to other existing and future transmission customers and resource owners

protest-er27-25-clean-energy-advocates.point: They note MISO's own account that LARS adopts no cost allocation methodology and defers cost shifting to later filings.
protest-er27-25-clean-energy-advocates.quote: LARS adopts no cost allocation methodology

protest-er27-25-clean-energy-advocates.point: Load-study and common violations go to Baseline Reliability or Other projects paid by all loads in the pricing zone, while DPP generators fund their own upgrades.
protest-er27-25-clean-energy-advocates.quote: LARS, therefore, takes a category of costs usually assigned to generators and assigns them to existing load.

protest-er27-25-clean-energy-advocates.point: They argue the standing injection persists after the paired load leaves, and zonal customers bear the cost.
protest-er27-25-clean-energy-advocates.quote: LARS creates a standing injection that was studied only on the assumption of a matched withdrawal

protest-er27-25-clean-energy-advocates.point: They say LARS would give a limited number of projects preferential access each year, with vertically integrated utilities deciding which.
protest-er27-25-clean-energy-advocates.quote: LARS sets up a generation and load study process that would offer a limited number of projects preferential access to the transmission system each year, year after year.

protest-er27-25-clean-energy-advocates.point: They say MISO invented an expansive definition of proximate instead of following the order's substation test.
protest-er27-25-clean-energy-advocates.quote: MISO invents a new expansive definition of "proximate" in an attempt to demonstrate that its proposal is responsive to the Commission's Order.

protest-er27-25-clean-energy-advocates.point: They argue siloed parallel processes raise upgrade costs and bias risk and favor integrated planning such as GALIP.
protest-er27-25-clean-energy-advocates.quote: meeting every new need with a new, siloed interconnection process (as MISO has done with ERAS, the ZGIA, now LARS, and soon the LLPR) significantly increases network upgrade costs

filing-er27-25-miso-lars.point: MISO asks for a December 2, 2026 effective date so it can start the first study period in Q1 2027.
filing-er27-25-miso-lars.quote: MISO requests that the Tariff revisions submitted herewith be made effective December 2, 2026

filing-er27-25-miso-lars.point: MISO says LARS responds to the show cause order finding on study procedures for electrically proximate large loads.
filing-er27-25-miso-lars.quote: MISO's existing Tariff may be unjust and unreasonable because it does not provide generator interconnection study procedures and services that account for the operational dynamics of serving electrically proximate large loads.

filing-er27-25-miso-lars.point: MISO moved the load threshold from 250 MW to 200 MW after stakeholder input.
filing-er27-25-miso-lars.quote: Stakeholders proposed alternative thresholds, including 200 MW, which MISO proposes herein

filing-er27-25-miso-lars.point: Load and generation studies run together and finish in about 120 days.
filing-er27-25-miso-lars.quote: The generation and load studies will be completed at the same time and will finish within approximately 120 days.

filing-er27-25-miso-lars.point: Only the Associated Transmission Customer, often a load-serving entity, can initiate an application, and a $250,000 non-refundable fee applies.
filing-er27-25-miso-lars.quote: A non-refundable fee of $250,000 must accompany the LARS Application and be paid by the LARS Associated Transmission Customer.

filing-er27-25-miso-lars.point: MISO takes ten applications per study period and runs three periods a year.
filing-er27-25-miso-lars.quote: There will be three LARS study periods each year and each study period will be completed in approximately 120 days

filing-er27-25-miso-lars.point: The generator is capped at 150 percent of the load's peak demand, and the pair must sit in one Local Resource Zone.
filing-er27-25-miso-lars.quote: limiting the amount of requested Interconnection Service to no more than 150% of the peak demand of the LARS Associated Load

filing-er27-25-miso-lars.point: MISO says costs from load-side and common violations go to Baseline Reliability or Other projects, and the pro forma cost shifting agreement follows by November 16, 2026.
filing-er27-25-miso-lars.quote: a pro forma cost shifting agreement will need to be executed and any new terms in transmission services agreements will need to be met.

filing-er27-25-miso-lars.point: Pairs must stay together for 15 years or the generator's LLGIA ends after a transition of up to one year.
filing-er27-25-miso-lars.quote: MISO will terminate the LLGIA after a limited operations transition period
